title: Financial Analyst (d/w/m)
descriptionHtml:
Our story:

Every year millions of people are either filing their taxes in fear or giving up on their tax refund altogether. We're working on fixing that. Our intuitive app enables anyone, regardless of education or background, to file their taxes with newfound confidence.

Spread across Germany, Spain and the UK, the team at Taxfix Group with its brands Taxfix and Steuerbot, is a compassionate group of solution-finders. We speak our minds openly, and with over 400 professionals, including tax experts, developers, and IT security experts, we're rich in ideas and voices. The group has facilitated more than 3.5 billion euros in tax refunds for its customers since its founding in 2016.

Your challenge

As Financial Analyst, Planning & Reporting Systems, you will build and maintain our planning and reporting models and dashboards, make sure data flows correctly from our source systems, and ensure the numbers the business relies on are accurate and consistent.

Alongside this, you will support core FP&A work such as forecasting, variance analysis and month-end reporting. The role reports to the Senior Director of FP&A and works closely with FinOps, Data and business stakeholders.


Your responsibilities

  • Build and maintain models in our planning platform, including dimensions, hierarchies and mapping tables, in line with the agreed model design

  • Build product P&Ls and product dashboards, and prepare the monthly reviews with commercial product owners

  • Monitor data flows from our ERP, HR and other source systems into the planning platform, and resolve issues together with FinOps and Data

  • Run monthly reconciliations between the planning platform, the general ledger and reported figures, and document the checks

  • Support the transition of planning and reporting workflows into the planning platform, in close collaboration with the FP&A team

  • Support FinOps on the interface between planning and consolidation, so management and statutory views reconcile

  • Maintain access rights, version control and model documentation

  • Support and train budget owners in using the platform for their planning and reporting

  • Automate recurring reports and workflows, using AI tools where they remove manual work

  • Support core FP&A processes when needed: monthly reporting, forecast updates, variance analysis and management materials

  • Deliver ad-hoc analysis on product performance to support commercial decisions

Your profile

  • 3+ years of experience in FP&A, controlling, finance systems or a similar analytical finance role, ideally in a fast-growing or subscription-based business; alternatively, a background as implementation consultant for Pigment, Anaplan or similar planning tools

  • Hands-on experience building models or reports in a modern planning tool (e.g. Pigment, Anaplan, Adaptive); Pigment experience is highly valued

  • Solid understanding of financial statements and accounting principles, with hands-on experience in budgeting, forecasting and variance analysis

  • Strong Excel skills and working knowledge of SQL; experience with ERP, consolidation or BI tools (e.g. NetSuite, LucaNet, Looker) is a plus

  • High attention to detail and care for data quality: you notice when a number does not tie, and you find out why

  • Hands-on use of AI in finance work (e.g. LLM assistants, AI features in finance and planning tools), and the curiosity to adopt new tools as they mature

  • Clear communicator, able to explain numbers to non-finance stakeholders

  • Structured, independent and pragmatic, with a strong sense of ownership

Why Taxfix? 

  • A chance to do meaningful, people-centric work with an international team of passionate professionals.

  • Holistic well-being with free mental health coaching sessions.

  • A monthly allowance to spend on an extensive range of services that you can use and roll over as flexibly as you like.

  • Employee stock options for all employees—because everyone deserves to benefit from the success they help to create.

  • 30 annual vacation days and flexible working hours.

  • A generous learning budget to support your personal and professional development and guidance from our internal L&D experts.

  • Work from abroad for up to six weeks every year. Just align with your team, and then enjoy your trip.

  • Plenty of opportunities to socialise as a team. In addition to internal meetups, our international team hosts regular get-togethers—virtually and in person when possible.

  • Free tax declaration filing, of course, through the Taxfix app—and internal support for all personal tax-related questions.

  • Have a four-legged friend in your life? We’re happy to have dogs join us in the office.


Excited? So are we. Check out our Life at Taxfix page on LinkedIn to get a glimpse of our culture.

At Taxfix, we believe that incredible things happen when you have a wealth of perspectives and experiences. We're proudly committed to equal employment and development opportunities no matter your gender, race, religion, age, sexual orientation, colour, disability, or place of origin. To help mitigate any potential unconscious biases, we ask that you refrain from including your picture, age, or marital status on your CV. Let your experiences speak for themselves.

Not sure if you meet all the requirements for this role? Please apply anyway. You might bring something special to the team that we hadn't considered previously.

title: Forward Deployed Engineering Manager
descriptionHtml:
As the Forward Deployed Engineering Manager, you will lead the team that puts Auterion's robotic systems to work with customers in the field. We build complete systems: vehicles, sensors, onboard compute, radio links, autonomy software, and ground control. Your job is to understand how all of it fits together and to make it work in real missions.

You will lead your team through the entire customer engagement, from discovery and integration to field trials and handover. You are not a hardware specialist. You are a systems engineer who can trace a problem across every layer of the system, lead people well, and earn the trust of demanding customers.

Responsibilities and Duties

  • Team Leadership & Mentorship: Lead and grow a cross-functional team of Forward Deployed Engineers covering systems integration and software. Hire, coach, and develop your engineers. Build a culture of ownership and proactive problem-solving.
  • Accountability: Keep the bar high for yourself and your team. Work directly with stakeholders across the company. You will have a close relationship with the CTO, CEO, VP of Engineering, and the engineering directors.
  • Field Deployment Oversight: Own technical delivery of customer deployments in demanding, non-standard environments. This covers system configuration, connectivity, mission readiness, and operation under environmental constraints.
  • System Integration: Act as the technical lead for high-stakes customer integrations. Ensure the full system works end to end: vehicle, payloads, onboard compute, communication links, autonomy software, and ground control.
  • Field Troubleshooting: Diagnose failures across hardware, firmware, software, and communications. Use logs, telemetry, and structured debugging to find root causes fast.
  • Stakeholder Management: Serve as the primary technical contact for defense and enterprise customers. Translate operational requirements into deployment plans that account for system performance, link quality, power, and mission constraints. Run technical meetings, demos, and field days.
  • Feedback Loop & Release Coordination: Work closely with Product and R&D to feed field results and real-world edge cases back into the product. Coordinate with R&D on platform releases so customer deployments stay current and stable.

Qualifications and Skills

  • Systems Engineering: 7+ years in technical roles in robotics, drones, autonomous vehicles, or comparable complex embedded systems. You understand the full system end to end and how a change in one subsystem affects the others.
  • Leadership Experience: 3+ years managing a technical, customer-facing team (Field Engineers, Forward Deployed Engineers, Solutions Architects, or similar). You have dealt with underperformance and built team culture deliberately.
  • Software Skills: Comfortable working in Linux. You write Python, read C++, and use Git. You debug from logs and telemetry, not only at the bench.
  • Hardware Fluency: You understand hardware at integration level: power, sensors, interfaces, and RF basics. You do not need to be a hardware designer.
  • Field Deployment Expertise: Hands-on experience with field-deployed systems where "turning it off and on again" isn't always an option. Understanding of networking and radio communication is a major plus.
  • Crisis Management: Proven ability to troubleshoot critical failures in the field under high pressure and with limited physical access to the hardware.
  • Customer Presence: Composure and credibility in front of demanding customers. You communicate clearly with engineers and decision-makers alike.
  • Languages: Fluent English. German is a strong plus.
  • Work Authorization: Must hold EU citizenship and be eligible to work in the European Union without restriction.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with PX4, ArduPilot, or ROS2
  • Background in defense or government programs
  • Eligibility for German security clearance

Benefits

  • Flexible working hours
  • Stock Options
  • Generous holiday allowance
  • Pension plan 
  • Extended social security package 
  • Enhanced maternity & paternity leave
  • Wellpass membership 

About Auterion

We are building the leading software platform for AI-powered autonomous systems for enterprise and government customers. Our team is supporting the most important missions and solving the most challenging problems.

At Auterion, we bring together the sharpest minds who love to solve the hardest problems. Join a vibrant team built on innovation, openness, and excellence, where you’ll be empowered to develop ideas, collaborate across all levels, and make an impact that matters.

title: Founding Business Development Representative
descriptionHtml:
TL;DR

We're hiring a Founding BDR to build Lovable's business development motion from the ground up. The job is to find, qualify and open the right accounts using a mix of your own outreach and the automation and AI agents you build to run alongside it. You'll own a pipeline number, work closely with our Account Executives globally and build a lot of your own tooling on Lovable itself. This is also how we develop AEs: perform here and you'll be running your own deals within 12 to 18 months. There's no playbook yet, so you'll be helping to write it.

Why Lovable?

Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we're just getting started.

We're building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.

Lovable is one of TIME's 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognised on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe's fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.

What we're looking for

  • Evidence you can generate pipeline. That could be as a BDR or SDR, a founder, in sales or revenue ops, or by building something that found its own customers. We care about the outcome more than the job title, and we'll ask to see it.

  • You already use AI and automation tooling (LLMs, Clay, n8n or similar) to research, personalise and sequence outreach, and you have opinions about what works and what doesn't.

  • You'd rather automate a repetitive workflow than keep doing it by hand, and you can show us something you've built.

  • Comfortable running outbound into named accounts and getting past the first contact to the people who actually make the decision.

  • Disciplined about qualifying out. A fast, well-reasoned no is a win for the business, and you don't chase volume for its own sake.

  • Able to explain a technical product in business terms to both technical and commercial buyers.

  • You set your own priorities, manage your own pipeline and hold yourself to account.

  • You want to become an Account Executive and are prepared to earn it.

  • Fluent English. A second European language (German, French, Spanish, Italian) is useful.

  • Experience with Lovable, developer tools or a product-led growth motion is a strong plus.

What you'll do

  • Design and run outbound systems: signal-based targeting, AI-assisted research, personalised sequences and automated workflows. Measure what converts and improve it every week.

  • Build internal GTM tooling on Lovable, such as enrichment flows, qualification agents and meeting-prep automations. The tooling you build is what the team after you will run on.

  • Qualify inbound demand quickly and thoroughly, and convert the right leads into well-prepared first meetings for the AE team.

  • Multi-thread into target accounts to reach economic buyers and technical decision-makers, not just the first person who replied.

  • Own a pipeline number and report clearly on how much comes from your own outreach versus automation, so we can scale both.

  • Work with the Account Executives you support on account plans, meeting prep and keeping deals moving between touchpoints.

  • Qualify out early and clearly when an account isn't a fit, so the team's time goes where it will pay off.

  • Feed what you're hearing from the market back to Sales, Marketing and Product to sharpen messaging and positioning.

Where this role goes

This is a development role with a defined path to Account Executive. We expect the people who join as BDRs now to form our next AE team.

  • Structured coaching from day one: weekly call reviews with experienced AEs and your manager, and a curriculum that covers discovery, demo, commercial negotiation and deal management.

  • The expectation that you progress to running your own deals within 12 to 18 months, based on performance rather than tenure.

  • As the first BDR at Lovable, real influence over how the role, the playbook and the tooling are defined for everyone who follows.

How we work

  • Based out of our London office Monday to Thursday, with the option to work from home on Fridays.

  • You'll work alongside a highly experienced team of Account Executives and your manager who will coach and support you day to day.

  • You'll have unlimited access to Lovable and whatever AI tooling you need to do the job, and the freedom to build what doesn't exist yet.

  • We'll measure you on pipeline created and meetings that convert, and on how much of that you've made repeatable for the people who come after you.

About your application

  • Please submit your application in English. It's our company language so you'll be speaking lots of it if you join.

title: Founding Engineer (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
The opportunity

Tax advisory runs on structured data, recurring work and clear rules, and almost none of it has been rebuilt with modern software. What decides who gets there first is real case data and engineers who build next to the people doing the work.

Vogel advises several thousand mid-sized companies and acquires established advisory firms, developing them further on one shared base. On top of the systems we buy, we build our own software: a data layer above DATEV, the tools our advisors use every day, and agents that take over recurring work. What counts is daily use, on data that is audited and closed.

As one of our first engineers, you build across the whole stack: data pipelines, backend, the interfaces advisors use and the agents on top. You take a problem from the first conversation with an advisor to software that runs every day. We are hiring our CTO in parallel, who will own the architecture and lead the team. You work directly with Moritz Vogel.

What you'll do

Tools advisors use

  • Sit with tax advisors and accountants on real cases, find where the work gets stuck, and turn it into software they use the next day. Your benchmark: an advisor would miss it if it were switched off.

  • Build interfaces, dashboards and internal tools, from the first prototype to something that runs without you.

  • Ship small and often: a tool in daily use beats a perfect plan.

Data and integration

  • Build the pipelines that move data out of DATEV and our other systems into our own data layer every night, checked from the first day.

  • Define every figure exactly once, so a number means the same thing in every tool and report.

  • Connect the systems each acquired firm brings, so one more firm never means one more integration project.

Agents and automation

  • Build agents that take over recurring work, with a clear line between what the model judges and what is calculated deterministically.

  • Make every result traceable by version, source and decision, so a certified professional can sign off on it.

  • Evaluate against closed, audited cases, not against test data.

Questions you'll answer

  • Which recurring task in an accounting team is the first one worth taking off people's hands, and how do you prove it?

  • How do you build fast now without leaving a mess for the next engineer?

  • When is a prototype ready to run on real data every day, and who signs off before it does?

What success looks like

  • 3 months: Your first tool is in daily use by an advisory team, and the nightly data load runs with checks.

  • 6 months: Several tools and the first agents run in regular operation. You own one area end to end, and others build on your code.

  • 12 months: You own a part of our software with its own users, and new engineers learn from your standards.

Where it leads: from engineer to owning a product area, as a senior engineer or by leading a team, decided by contribution, not by years served.

What you bring

  • A degree in computer science, mathematics, physics, engineering or a related field from a strong university such as TUM, or an equally strong record of your own projects.

  • You have shipped software that other people used, at work, as a working student or in your own project.

  • You write production code in at least one language, ideally Python or TypeScript, and you are at home with SQL and relational databases.

  • AI is your everyday tool: you write, review and test code with it, and you know where it goes wrong.

  • You want breadth across data, backend, interface and agents, and you work in German and in person, because our advisors and clients do.

  • You learn from practitioners, and you set the highest standard in everything you ship, not because someone checks, but because mediocrity bothers you.

A plus, not a requirement

  • One to two years as an engineer in a young startup or scale-up, or a working-student role where you owned something real.

  • Knowledge of accounting, tax or DATEV, or data pipelines and agents you have run in production.

  • No conventional CV required: a mathematician or physicist who builds, an information systems graduate with a real engineering track, or the founder of a small product. We assess contribution, not labels. The range shown is not room for negotiation but a profile scale: the lower end stands for starting right after university, the upper third for someone who already carries the standard work of the role on their own. A different background starts at a different market price and converges on the role's level after twelve months of proven performance.

What this role is and what it isn't

  • Building on a running business, not a greenfield. DATEV runs and clients do not wait. What you build has to work next to daily operations.

  • An operating company, not a software vendor. The users are our own teams. What we build and in which order is decided together with management; you shape how.

  • Breadth, not a specialist track. If you want to perfect one layer for years, this is the wrong role.

Why join us

  • Real data and real users from the first day. Decades of audited, closed work, and advisors who use what you ship the same week.

  • Leverage through acquisitions. Every firm that joins Vogel runs on what you build.

  • Close to the decisions. You work directly with management and see what gets built and why. Hierarchical in decisions, flat in communication, autonomous in execution. Performance is celebrated, not hidden, without politics and without consensus theater.

  • Substance behind you. A profitable, growing business. No funding round decides whether your work continues.

The FAQ below is in German, as is our working day.

FAQ

1. Was ist Vogel – und wo arbeitet ihr?

Vogel ist eine der führenden Mittelstandsberatungen Deutschlands – seit 1959, inhabergeführt in zweiter Generation, mit eigenem Kapital – und baut daraus die führende Beratungsplattform für den Mittelstand. Wir arbeiten an drei Standorten: Aalen als gewachsenem Stammsitz, Bopfingen im Kerngeschäft und München als neuem Hub. An allen dreien suchen wir quer durch die Funktionen – von Steuerberatung über Beratung bis zu den Teams, die das Fundament darunter bauen.

2. Wie sind die Gehaltsbänder zu verstehen?

Bewusst breit – und an jeder Stelle ausgewiesen, bevor du dich bewirbst. Wir differenzieren nach Track Record und Marktwert, nicht nach Abschluss: knappe, stark gefragte Profile am oberen Ende, weniger knappe am unteren. Die ausgewiesene Spanne ist kein Verhandlungsspielraum, sondern eine Profil-Skala – zwei Menschen mit ähnlicher Erfahrung können bei uns unterschiedlich verdienen. Was das obere Ende bestimmt, ist der Reifegrad, nicht die Zahl der Berufsjahre und nicht das Verhandlungsgeschick.

3. Wie viel – und wie – wird bei Vogel gearbeitet?

Gemessen wird an dem, was du bewegst, nicht an Stunden. Ehrlich ist aber auch: Wer 9-to-5 sucht, ist bei uns nicht die erste Adresse. Wir suchen Menschen, die aus eigenem Antrieb intensiv arbeiten, weil die Aufgaben es wert sind. Wie du deine Zeit verteilst, ist weitgehend deine Sache. Was wir teilen: Wir arbeiten präsent zusammen und sehen uns im Normalfall täglich im Büro – Kultur, Sparring und die besten Ideen entstehen in der täglichen Nähe. Wir sind keine Remote-Company und haben keine großen Home-Office-Policies; einzelne Remote-Tage sind kein Problem.

4. Wie läuft die Bewerbung?

Schlank, schnell, transparent – und nach Profil gestaffelt. In der Regel sind es vier Schritte: eine schriftliche Aufgabe, in der du zu acht Fragen Position beziehst – KI ist ausdrücklich erlaubt, wir bitten nur um eine kurze Selbstauskunft dazu; ein Gespräch von einer halben Stunde; eine gemeinsame Arbeitssitzung an einem echten Problem aus unserem Alltag; und ein Termin vor Ort mit dem Team und gemeinsamem Essen. Wie viele Schritte es tatsächlich werden, hängt von der Rolle ab: Bei Praktikum und Werkstudium fällt der Vor-Ort-Termin weg, für Schülerjobs genügt ein Gespräch, bei Senior-Rollen kommt ein gemeinsamer Arbeitsnachmittag dazu. Vorab kannst du einen Zehn-Minuten-Call buchen, in dem nur du fragst. In der Regel hörst du nach jedem Schritt innerhalb von 48 Stunden von uns.

5. Wie funktioniert die variable Vergütung?

Quartalsweise an Leistung gekoppelt, qualitativ bewertet. Die Skala steigt mit dem Level: bis 20 % Associate, 27,5 % Manager, 35 % Senior Manager, 42,5 % Director, 50 % VP. Erwartungswert bei guter Leistung – du erfüllst die Anforderungen, setzt eigene Akzente, bestehst den Keeper Test – liegt bei rund 50 % des Maximums; der Maximalbonus ist nicht der Normalfall. Im Fokus steht eine ganzheitliche Beurteilung durch deine Führungskraft anhand von sechs Kriterien: Impact, Judgement, Communication, Execution, Growth und Values.

6. Wie entwickle ich mich – welche Karrierewege gibt es?

Zwei aktive Wege: die IC-Karriere (fachliche Tiefe, Expertenlaufbahn) über die Stufen Expert, Senior, Lead und Principal – und die Management-Karriere (Führung, Personalverantwortung) über Manager, Senior Manager, Director und VP. Beide werden gleich vergütet, und beide müssen nicht nach oben führen: Wer auf einer Stufe bleibt und dort weiter in die Tiefe geht, ist bei uns genauso richtig. Die Richtung wählst du nach dem Onboarding, meist in Jahr 1–3. Berufseinstieg ist kein Sonderweg, sondern der frühe Teil derselben Strecke – vom Werkstudenten oder Praktikanten zum Associate, für die Besten ohne erneutes Bewerbungsverfahren.

7. Team, Kultur, Urlaub?

Das gemeinsame Mittagessen ist der tägliche Ankerpunkt – wer im Büro ist, isst mit; erwartet, nicht kontrolliert. Das Abendessen ist dasselbe Angebot ohne jede Erwartung. Beides ohne Eigenanteil. Dazu Social Events und Offsites in regelmäßigem Rhythmus – nicht als Pflichtprogramm, sondern weil ein gutes Team auch abseits der Arbeit Zeit teilt.

Benefits sind bei uns nicht das Sahnehäubchen, sondern das, was Intensität über Jahre tragbar macht: Examensförderung mit 25.000 EUR Qualifizierungsbudget und drei Monaten Freistellung, 100-prozentige Übernahme der Kinderbetreuung, EGYM Wellpass, betriebliche Altersvorsorge, Job-Ticket mit 90 % Zuschuss, Homeoffice-Ausstattung und ein Gerät deiner Wahl aus unserem Katalog, ein Buch im Monat aus dem Vogel-Kanon – und KI-Tools ohne Token-Limit und ohne Budgetdeckel. Urlaub: 28 Tage.

title: Founding Enterprise BDR | France
descriptionHtml:
about us

Every 10 minutes, 18 million conversations happen between businesses and consumers around the world.

For decades, the consumer side of those conversations sucked: long queues, robotic menus, repeated explanations, and advice that is often unhelpful. Most people today still cannot simply say what their problem is in natural language when communicating with businesses.

AI changes that. For the first time, companies can have natural conversations with customers at massive scale. Every B2C company - from energy providers to telcos to insurers - will use AI agents to talk to their customers. The number of conversations businesses will handle is going to explode in the coming years.

At telli, we are solving the challenges that come with that shift. Today, leading B2C companies like Sky are already using telli to deploy thousands of voice agents to provide their customers with a new experience. But building a first voice agent is easy, getting it to drive real outcomes for customers and businesses is the hard part. telli helps companies build, deploy, and improve consumer-facing AI voice agents at scale. This will become one of the most important software categories of the next decade, and we intend to win it.

We are a small, AI-pilled team that likes to solve hard problems. Be it engineering, product, or GTM - we build, experiment, and move fast, while heavily leveraging the capabilities of AI models. All of us like to challenge ourselves and take real ownership over what we do, all while still staying humble and keeping a low-ego culture.

Check out our principles to see how we work.

Your mission

telli is arriving in France. We are building a small, mighty team in Paris to make every customer interaction worth having. The product is real; the French playbook is still being written. We are outsiders here, and we will earn our place through better conversations, sharper execution, and customers who see the difference.

We are outbound first. As our founding BDR in France, you will start conversations rather than wait for them. You will find the right companies, reach the people who own customer operations, and create qualified opportunities for the team. You will also help decide which messages, channels, and routines deserve to become our French sales playbook.

What you'll do

  • Build targeted account lists and find the people with a real customer interaction problem to solve.

  • Prospect every day through calls, email, LinkedIn, and thoughtful experiments. The phone is a core part of this role.

  • Run sharp first conversations: understand the workflow, volume, owner, urgency, and reason to act; then hand over opportunities with context the AE can use.

  • Test messages and sequences, measure what turns into useful conversations and qualified pipeline, and improve quickly.

  • Bring what prospects say back to the France team, product, and marketing, and use those insights to improve targeting and messaging.

What makes you a great fit

  • You do not need sales experience. Your background could be the military, firefighting, competitive sport, or something else entirely. What matters is your discipline, coachability, rigor, and ability to keep going through rejection.

  • You speak clearly, listen closely, are curious about how businesses work, and are willing to learn a technical product. You are comfortable picking up the phone.

  • You care about the quality of the opportunity, not just the number of meetings on a calendar.

title: FPGA Engineer - Radar
descriptionHtml:
About Alta Ares


Alta Ares is an air defense Neoprime. We build AI-guided interceptors to counter drones and cruise missiles, along with the software platform that powers them.

Our customers are NATO-aligned militaries and defense institutions, and our systems are regularly deployed during live exercises and operational demonstrations across Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.

Founded in 2024, we have grown to 160 people, raised over $60M, and increased revenue 40× this year. We are now entering a new phase of international expansion, industrial scaling, fundraising, and product development.

Role & Mission

  • Turn radar sensing requirements into FPGA designs that support reliable drone detection in operational conditions.

  • Define how radar data is acquired, processed, and delivered to the rest of the system, working across RF, electronics, and software teams.

  • Establish processing budgets and select implementation approaches based on detection performance, latency, numerical accuracy, and available FPGA resources.

  • Develop reference models to study radar behavior in noise and clutter and guide hardware design decisions.

  • Build reusable RTL functions for waveform generation and receive processing in FMCW and pulsed radar systems.

  • Implement the processing stages needed to extract targets from radar returns, including matched filtering, pulse compression, range-Doppler processing, clutter rejection, and CFAR detection.

  • Integrate ADC/DAC interfaces, coordinate transmit and receive timing, and ensure synchronization with the radar front end.

  • Specify how detections and associated measurements are passed to tracking functions and embedded software.

  • Verify designs against reference models through automated testbenches and hardware-in-the-loop testing.

  • Investigate performance gaps on target hardware and use laboratory measurements and field results to improve the processing chain.

  • Document design decisions, interfaces, and validation results to support integration and future product development.


Candidate Profile

  • At least three years of FPGA development experience, with practical exposure to radar or sonar processing.

  • Ability to take a signal-processing function from an algorithmic description to verified RTL in VHDL or Verilog/SystemVerilog.

  • Strong DSP foundations, including FFT, digital filtering, windowing, and the effects of quantization and fixed-point precision.

  • Understanding of how radar systems estimate target range and velocity, distinguish returns from clutter, and set detection thresholds.

  • Working knowledge of matched filtering, pulse compression, range-Doppler maps, and CFAR techniques.

  • Familiarity with FMCW and pulsed radar, including the relationship between waveform choices, acquisition timing, and digital processing.

  • Experience assessing radar performance through simulation, including signal-to-noise ratio and clutter effects.

  • Experience developing testbenches, debugging FPGA hardware, and validating processing chains with hardware-in-the-loop methods.

  • Master’s degree or equivalent in Electrical Engineering, Signal Processing, Applied Physics, or a related field.

Skills & Qualities

  • Hands-on engineer motivated by making radar processing work reliably on physical hardware.

  • Able to connect system-level performance issues with their causes in algorithms, RTL, interfaces, or timing.

  • Methodical approach to debugging, verification, and documenting technical decisions.

  • Comfortable owning development tasks and coordinating integration work across disciplines.

  • Clear communicator who makes trade-offs explicit and flags risks early.

  • Entrepreneurial mindset with the ability to operate autonomously in a fast-growing company.

  • High integrity and professionalism in handling sensitive defense technologies.

title: Fullstack Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Want to join a team of passionate people who want to build a future where no one dies from skin cancer?

👋 About us

We're an AI Health Tech company in the UK and Europe, leading from the front in the AI Diagnostics space.

Our AI Platform, DERM, is the UK’s and Europe’s first autonomous Class III AI as a medical device, certified to the same safety standard as a pacemaker. Independently proven to perform at least as well as a face-to-face dermatologist assessment, our technology is giving millions of people access to a fast and accurate way to detect skin cancer, saving significant time and costs for global healthcare systems and improving outcomes for patients. DERM has been an integrated part of NHS dermatology pathways for over six years and is already in use in 25 NHS Trusts, and trusted by private health providers including Bupa and Vitality. It has assessed over 300,000 patients and found more than 25,000 cancers, validated by histopathology, the diagnostic gold standard.

We are fast growing, raised £15M in series B funding in 2025, and are scaling across Europe - with regulatory approvals underway in other regions. In June 2026, we launched DERM Zero, the world' s first Class III regulated medical device technology to deliver autonomous clinical grade skin cancer assessments from a smartphone, changing the way that people can access clinically validated skin cancer checks.

title: Functioneel applicatiebeheerder Backend Platform
descriptionHtml:
Bouw jij mee aan betrouwbaar functioneel beheer voor applicaties die onze collega’s dagelijks nodig hebben?

Wie ben jij

Je vindt het leuk om je vast te bijten in applicaties en processen en neemt technische kennis mee. Wanneer een gebruiker met een vraag of probleem komt, wil jij niet alleen weten hoe je het oplost, maar ook begrijpen waar het vandaan komt.

Je beweegt gemakkelijk tussen business en IT. Je kunt met een gebruiker praten over een bedrijfsproces en vervolgens met technische collega's of een leverancier bepalen wat er nodig is om een probleem op te lossen of een verbetering te realiseren.

Daarnaast kijk je verder dan je eigen applicatie. Je begrijpt dat systemen steeds meer met elkaar verbonden zijn en houdt daarom rekening met afhankelijkheden binnen de gehele keten.

We vinden het belangrijk dat je:

  • HBO werk- en denkniveau hebt, bij voorkeur met een relevante opleiding;

  • ervaring hebt met applicatiebeheer of een vergelijkbare functie;

  • affiniteit hebt met bedrijfsprocessen en informatiesystemen;

  • gebruikersvragen en problemen kunt analyseren en vertalen naar effectieve oplossingen;

  • ervaring hebt met het testen en implementeren van wijzigingen;

  • oog hebt voor de samenhang tussen applicaties, processen en IT-ketens;

  • ervaring hebt met Agile werken;

  • initiatief neemt, verantwoordelijkheid pakt en proactief handelt;

  • helder communiceert en gemakkelijk samenwerkt met gebruikers, IT-collega's en leveranciers.

Ervaring met applicaties of processen binnen Finance, Verzekeringen of HR is een pré. Denk bijvoorbeeld aan CODA, Crescendo, QIS of AFAS. Je hoeft ze zeker niet allemaal te kennen. We vinden het vooral belangrijk dat je ervaring hebt met applicatiebeheer en je nieuwe applicaties en bedrijfsprocessen snel eigen kunt maken.

Wat ga je doen

Als Functioneel Applicatiebeheerder ben jij een belangrijke schakel tussen gebruikers, de business, IT-teams en leveranciers. Je zorgt ervoor dat applicaties en IT-diensten betrouwbaar functioneren en dat gebruikers goed worden ondersteund. Je werkt aan zowel de dagelijkse operatie als aan de verdere professionalisering van het beheer. Afhankelijk van jouw kennis, ervaring en de behoefte binnen Backend Platform kun je bijvoorbeeld werken aan applicaties binnen Finance, Verzekeringen of HR.


Je werkzaamheden bestaan onder andere uit:

  • functioneel beheren en ondersteunen van één of meerdere bedrijfskritische applicaties;

  • behandelen en analyseren van functionele vragen, incidenten en verstoringen;

  • bewaken van de goede werking en continuïteit van applicaties;

  • analyseren van gewenste wijzigingen en bepalen wat deze betekenen voor de applicatie en de omliggende keten;

  • afstemmen met gebruikers, leveranciers en IT-collega's over problemen, oplossingen en verbeteringen;

  • ondersteunen bij het realiseren en implementeren van wijzigingen;

  • voorbereiden, coördineren en uitvoeren van functionele en ketentesten;

  • bewaken dat wijzigingen correct en beheerst in gebruik worden genomen;

  • signaleren van mogelijkheden om processen, applicaties en het gebruik daarvan verder te verbeteren;

  • vastleggen en delen van kennis over applicaties, processen en werkwijzen.

Wat bieden wij

Bij Univé IT bieden we je een uitdagende functie binnen een dynamische organisatie, waarin je veel ruimte krijgt om mee te bouwen aan professioneel en toekomstgericht applicatiebeheer.

  • Veel ruimte voor eigen initiatief, eigenaarschap en vakinhoudelijke ontwikkeling.

  • Nauwe samenwerking met ervaren collega’s binnen IT, architectuur, security en waardestromen.

  • De mogelijkheid om actief bij te dragen aan de verdere professionalisering van IT Kern.

  • Ruimte om mee te denken over marktontwikkelingen, automatisering en de inzet van AI binnen Unive en IT.

Arbeidsvoorwaarden

  • Jaarsalaris van € 51.777 tot € 71.907 bruto per jaar op basis van 38 uur, inclusief vakantiegeld en dertiende maand en exclusief variabele beloning;

  • Dienstverband van 32 tot 38 uur per week;

  • Standplaats Zwolle of Assen, met hybride werken in overleg met het team;

  • Een contract voor bepaalde tijd met uitzicht op een vast contract;

  • 13e maand en 8% vakantiegeld;

  • Variabele collectieve prestatiebeloning van maximaal 9% van het jaarsalaris;

  • 26 vakantiedagen bij een 38-urige werkweek;

  • Goede pensioen- en studiekostenregeling;

  • Thuiswerk- en reiskostenvergoeding;

  • Korting op schade- en zorgverzekeringen bij Univé.

Wie wij zijn

Univé is een coöperatieve organisatie die dicht bij haar leden staat. Als IT-organisatie werken we aan een wendbaar, betrouwbaar, veilig en toekomstgericht IT-landschap. Schaalbare technologie, goede processen, standaardisatie en continu verbeteren zijn daarbij belangrijk. Binnen IT Kern werken verschillende teams aan het beheren, ondersteunen en doorontwikkelen van applicaties, platformen, infrastructuur, netwerkdiensten en securityoplossingen. Deze IT-diensten zijn essentieel voor onze dagelijkse dienstverlening aan leden en voor de ondersteuning van onze collega’s. Samen bouwen we aan een moderne IT-organisatie waarin we betrouwbaar functioneren, waardestromen goed worden ondersteund en vernieuwing gecontroleerd en toekomstbestendig kan plaatsvinden. Je komt terecht in een team waarin samenwerking, eigenaarschap en plezier in het werk belangrijk zijn. We werken met collega’s die graag verbeteren, verantwoordelijkheid nemen en elkaar helpen om het applicatie- en IT-landschap iedere dag een stukje beter te maken.

For more information, please visit www.vml.com and follow along on  LinkedIn #WeAreVML.

You will be responsible for turning the most valuable market signals, client relationships, and WPP network intelligence into high-quality, strategically shaped growth opportunities and for creating the momentum that moves them from first conversation to qualified pursuit.

Operating at the intersection of consultative selling, transformation strategy, and executive relationship management, you will bring a rare combination of commercial instinct and intellectual rigour. title: Google Cloud Data Platform and Security Architect
descriptionHtml:
About Intelance

Intelance is an independent technology, AI and cyber assurance firm based in the UK. We help organisations check, govern and improve their technology through enterprise architecture, AI governance, cyber assurance and data governance work. We are building a small panel of senior associates to deliver technology and AI due diligence on company sales and investments.

The role

You will review the security and set up of Google Cloud data platforms as part of technology due diligence, for clients who are selling, buying or investing in software companies. Buyers want to know that client data is kept apart, that access is tightly controlled and logged, and that the security claims in a company's SOC 2 or ISO 27001 evidence hold up in practice.

You report to an Intelance engagement partner and work with our technology due diligence lead, who brings your findings into the final report.

What you will do

  • Review how Google Cloud projects, BigQuery datasets and storage are organised, and how each client's data is kept separate.

  • Check IAM roles, service accounts, network controls, secrets and encryption keys.

  • Check logging, monitoring and alerting, including who can reach production data and how that access is recorded.

  • Test security claims against the company's SOC 2, ISO 27001 or client security questionnaire evidence.

  • Review backup, recovery and how the platform copes as data and users grow.

  • Rate each finding by how it could affect the deal, and write clear, practical fixes.

What you will bring

  • At least five years designing, running or securing production platforms on Google Cloud.

  • Hands on knowledge of BigQuery, IAM, VPC Service Controls, Cloud Logging and Cloud KMS.

  • A current Google Cloud Professional certification is a strong plus.

  • Experience supporting SOC 2 or ISO 27001 audits.

  • Clear, plain writing that founders, buyers and lawyers can follow.

  • Experience with health or other regulated data, or with due diligence work, is a strong plus.

How the work is set up

  • Remote within the UK, with occasional meetings in London.

  • Around 3 to 5 days between late November 2026 and the end of January 2027, with further engagements as the practice grows.

  • Freelance, or through your own limited company, at £600 to £750 a day depending on experience. Reasonable travel costs for client meetings are covered.

  • A panel agreement, NDA and statement of work are signed before any client details are shared.

  • You work from an Intelance mailbox and use our evidence log and report templates, so every report meets the same standard.

How to apply

Send your CV and answer the short screening questions. They take about two minutes. We aim to reply to every shortlisted candidate within five working days.

title: Graphene Device Physics Modeling Expert (f/m/d)
descriptionHtml:
About us

We see the semiconductor industry as a realm of possibility. We see opportunity. We see the profound impact that our graphene solutions will have in transforming the industry. We invite you to join us in driving change with our fundamentally human-centered approach, uniting bright minds around a shared vision. The vision is: Prove to everybody that you can make a fundamental change. Prove with your knowledge and skills how things can be done differently. Together, we can change the paradigm of how the world connects

About our technology

The semiconductor industry’s growing demand for more powerful chips with higher bandwidth and lower power finds its solution in our technology. We connect chips to high-throughput, low-delay computing networks. The key lies in harnessing the physical properties of graphene to combine electronic computing with photonic communication, allowing countless chips to interact almost as if they were one. Our graphene photonic innovation increases computing power and efficiency to a new order of magnitude

In short, we connect chips to create powerful and energy-efficient networks, overcoming connectivity limitations in the semiconductor industry. We deliver the graphene solution

 

The Role

We are looking for a Graphene Device Physics Modeling Expert, to develop and refine physics based models for graphene photonic devices. Working at the intersection of research and software development you will translate state-of-the-art research into reliable simulation capabilities that support device design and development.

To join our team, you should be excited to:

  • Research the literature on state-of-the-art approaches to graphene device modeling and simulation

  • Work with commercial TCAD and multiphysics simulation tools

  • Translate physical models from scientific literature into robust, maintainable Python code

  • Develop and extend models for graphene-based photonic devices, incorporating new physical effects and functionalities

  • Calibrate, validate, and refine models using experimental characterization data

  • Collaborate closely with various teams, prioritizing modeling activities in line with team and company goals

  • Document your work clearly and contribute to shared software-development practices

Your Qualifications

  • PhD in Physics, Materials Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field

  • Strong foundation in solid-state physics, semiconductor physics, and mathematics

  • Proficient in modeling techniques and methodologies for semiconductor physics

  • Proven ability to translate scientific literature and mathematical models into simulation code

  • Experience with TCAD development

  • Proficiency in Python and Git

  • Experience solving partial differential equations, particularly for charge and heat transport

  • Experience with graphene and photonics

  • Experience with commercial simulation tools such as COMSOL Multiphysics or Ansys Lumerical is a plus

Our work culture

People Over Processes. At Black Semiconductor, flexibility is key—we ensure work adapts to life, not the other way around. We champion work-life harmony, where careers are meaningful and enriching. Our processes are human-centric, allowing you to focus on what matters

Your Health and Future Matter. Your well-being is paramount. We offer a comprehensive benefits package with outstanding insurance, pension and virtual stock options for your mental, physical, and financial health. Your peace of mind is our priority - in the present and future

We Live Openness. Collaboration and inclusivity are the cornerstones of our culture. We practice openness, fostering trust and respect. Individuality is our collective strength, fueling innovation and driving us forward

We connect chips – and people. We encourage qualified individuals from any background to apply. We foster an inclusive and supportive work environment that values collaboration, innovation, and growth. Join our team and be part of an organization dedicated to making a difference in the industry

descriptionHtml:

Street Group is one of the fastest-growing PropTech companies in the UK. We want to be the leading creator of delightful experiences for everybody involved in buying, selling, renting and letting property, regardless of their involvement, to improve the industry for everybody by elevating UK Estate Agencies through world-class technology.


We're moving towards ISO certification for security, with SOC 2 and other standards likely to follow as we expand into new markets. Getting there - and staying there - takes dedicated documentation, tracking and governance, and that's where you come in. We're looking for a GRC Lead to own the frameworks, audits and evidence that prove we do what we say we do, working alongside our Security & Resilience Lead as we grow this function.


This is a genuinely flat, cross-functional role. You'll work directly with sales, marketing and engineering with no layers of hierarchy between you and the people who hold the information you need. You'll have real autonomy in how you run the audit programme.


Here's what you can expect to be working on as our GRC Lead

  • Work with teams across the business to produce business continuity plans in a standardised format.

  • Support customer due diligence and KYC checks - particularly important in the payment space - and formalise this into a robust, business-as-usual process, alongside supporting contract reviews.

  • Keep on top of the legal and regulatory landscape, translating incoming legislation into a clear playbook for teams well ahead of time.

  • Own our data classification framework, privacy policies, information asset register and records of processing.

  • Map how data flows through the business, risk-assess critical processes as an independent party, and maintain the corporate risk register - standardising how risk, including impacts, are scored and reported to stakeholders.

  • Keep our governance documentation, policies and knowledge repositories standardised, version-controlled and free of duplication.

  • Build and run an efficient annual internal audit programme across every part of the business, from sales to finance to physical security.

  • Support FAQs, RFIs and marketing reviews with up-to-date evidence from your audits, and coordinate physical and environmental audits and annual service reviews.

Why you should (and shouldn't) apply

You should apply if:

  • You'd rather enable good practice across a business than dictate it from an ivory tower - you know how to get buy-in, not just compliance.

  • You want breadth: you'll work with sales, marketing, engineering and finance, genuinely cross-functional rather than siloed in one team.

  • You want the autonomy to choose your own approach to audit and governance, as long as it's effective and efficient.

  • You're comfortable holding people accountable - the worst thing you could do here is let something slide because it's easier than having a difficult conversation.


You probably shouldn't apply if:

  • You need everything mapped out for you - part of the role is choosing how you run your own audit programme.

  • You're not open to new ideas and continual improvement.

  • You're looking for a technical security role only - that's a different hire; this one is about governance, documentation and people.

  • You'd rather work with one team than build relationships and trust across the whole business.


A bit about you

  • Solid experience in Governance, Risk and Compliance, with knowledge of compliance frameworks such as ISO 27001.

  • Comfortable working with data and information, with a good understanding of data privacy and information governance principles.

  • A confident communicator who's trusted by the people they work with - you'll be sitting with sales, marketing and engineering just as often as with the security team, so relationships and trust matter as much as technical depth.

  • Excellent attention to detail, with strong documentation and organisational skills - much of this role is about producing evidence, policies and reports that stand up to scrutiny.

  • Calm under challenge - open to discussing new ways of working even about your own processes and systems.


Research has shown that women tend to rule themselves out of applying for jobs unless they meet 100% of the requirements. If you fall into that category and are about to rule yourself out based on the above criteria, please consider applying anyway. We'd love to see your application.

STRATOS was built to solve this problem. We work with global B2B companies to synchronize strategy and execution and ensure commercial success is driven by potential, not gut feel or old data.

STRATOS is a category-defining, rapidly growing startup, profitable and majority founder-owned with our Series A still ahead of us, funded by high-profile investors (e.g., Accel) and trusted by 15 global industrial leaders and Fortune 500 customers. Our software integrates complex datasets into a unified solution, combining deep data integration, best-in-class workflows, and cutting-edge generative AI.

The role

You own how we reach the commercial leaders at Europe’s largest manufacturers, and whether they reply. You plan and run the campaigns, make the calls, write the sequences, build the materials that get someone into a room, and keep the pipeline numbers our CRO takes to the board. You do all of it with AI tooling that lets one person cover what used to take a team, and you work directly with the CEO, CRO and CMO on what to try next.

Tasks

  • Run campaigns end to end. Plan, launch, and optimise outreach campaigns. Write, test, measure, iterate.

  • Own outbound. Run cold calling, email sequences, and LinkedIn programmes targeting commercial leaders at Europe’s largest manufacturers, armed with the AI-recommended warm intro paths and account intelligence.

  • Drive our paid channels. Organise, launch, and optimise paid campaigns, from targeting and creative through to spend decisions and attribution.

  • Build materials that win meetings. Produce client documents, demos, and interactive presentations from our library of high-end content, using our templates and AI tooling. Fast turnaround, senior-team standard.

  • Keep the engine clean. Log your activity, keep pipeline data spotless in HubSpot, and produce the weekly pipeline, coverage, and forecast numbers the CRO uses to manage the number and brief the board.

  • Make our commercial engine sharper every week. New plays, new automations, new content for the library. What you build compounds.

  • Use AI as a force multiplier. We are an AI-first company. You will use our AI tooling and automations to do the work of a team several times your size.

Who this is for

Most people who do well here have one to three years behind them in growth, sales development or commercial execution at a B2B software company, or a strategy background and a clear preference for doing the work over advising on it.

  • You have run outreach yourself and can tell us the numbers: how many you sent, what came back, and what you changed when it didn’t work.

  • You write well under constraint. Most of this job is persuading a busy executive in four sentences, and you know the difference between a cold email that lands and one that gets deleted unread.

  • You reach for automation before you reach for repetition. HubSpot, Sales Navigator, sequencing tools and modern AI tooling are things you have used already, or will teach yourself over a weekend.

  • You measure yourself on meetings booked and pipeline created.

  • You are comfortable hearing that your campaign didn’t work, and quick to change it.

This probably isn’t for you if you want a defined remit, a marketing role one step removed from the phone, or a job where someone else owns the number.

What we offer

  • Equity through our stock option programme, so you share in the long-term success and growth of the company

  • A highly competitive salary

  • Direct access to Fortune 500 executives from your first months, at a level most people wait a decade for

  • Work alongside former MBB consultants and Fortune 500 executives who will teach you directly — our team is small enough that this happens in person, not through a training curriculum

  • Private healthcare

  • Pension scheme

  • 25 days of annual leave, plus bank holidays

  • Work from abroad — up to four weeks a year, and up to two weeks at a time

  • Hybrid office policy, with visa sponsorship available

  • A company committed to social and environmental responsibility — we pledge to be a net-zero CO₂ company and donate 1% of our revenue to social causes

Practicalities

  • London-based, 3 days a week in our Farringdon office

The process

  1. First round with our Talent Lead — 30 minutes

  1. Hiring Manager interviews with CRO – 30 minutes

  1. Stakeholder interview with CMO – 30 minutes

  1. Final interview with CEO – 30 minutes

title: Growth Manager / Senior Growth Manager (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
Portfolio, Wachstums-Roadmap und Go-to-Market für Cloud-, Daten-, KI- und SaaS-Lösungen – du machst Marketing und Vertrieb im deutschsprachigen Mittelstand noch erfolgreicher.

Über Coduct Group

Die Coduct-Gruppe verbindet Technologieberatung, Umsetzung und eigene Produkte unter einem Dach. Seit 2017 begleiten wir Unternehmen bei der Modernisierung ihrer IT-Systeme, Plattformen und Cloud-Architekturen – von der Analyse über Entwicklung und Migration bis zum Betrieb.

  • Die Marke Coduct (Kamp-Lintfort, Berlin, Ho-Chi-Minh-City): IT-Beratung und Softwareentwicklung für Cloud, Daten, KI und Automatisierung; auch als Build-Operate-Transfer-Modell (BOT)

  • Die Marke ainavio: unsere SaaS-Plattform für Produktinformationsmanagement (PIM)

  • Die Marke Code Leap: unsere Software-Engineering-Marke

Als Microsoft CSP-Partner und dreifach zertifizierter Microsoft Solutions Partner (Data & AI, Digital & App Innovation, Infrastructure/Azure) kombinieren wir Lizenzierung, Beratung und Umsetzung aus einer Hand. Zu unseren Kunden gehören Energieversorger, ERP- und Softwareanbieter, Handel und E-Commerce sowie Industrieunternehmen – darunter JTL, Netze BW, Schleupen und Galeria.

Warum wir diese Rolle jetzt besetzen

Wir stehen an der Schwelle zur nächsten Wachstumsphase. Dafür haben wir die Unternehmensfunktion Growth geschaffen, geführt von unserem VP Growth. Growth plant das Wachstum der Gruppe und sorgt dafür, dass es gelingt: Wir entwickeln Portfolio und Wachstums-Roadmap und befähigen Marketing und Vertrieb, Wachstum zu realisieren.

Wichtig: Growth ist kein zweiter Vertrieb – aber Growth jagt. Nach dem Hunting-Prinzip spürst du Wachstumschancen aktiv auf und bringst sie gemeinsam mit dem Vertrieb zum Abschluss. Kundenbeziehungen liegen beim Vertrieb; du sorgst dafür, dass er die richtigen Angebote, Argumente und Werkzeuge hat – und dass aus ersten Aufträgen langfristige Kundenbeziehungen werden.

Deine Aufgaben

1. Wachstumsstrategie & Growth-Roadmap

  • Du entwickelst mit dem VP Growth eine mehrjährige Growth-Roadmap mit klaren Etappen, Prioritäten und Meilensteinen

  • Du jagst aktiv Wachstumschancen – neue Segmente, Partnerschaften (u. a. Microsoft), Großchancen bei Neu- und Bestandskunden – und bringst sie gemeinsam mit dem Vertrieb zum Abschluss

  • Du bewertest Zielsegmente und validierst neue Geschäftsfelder schnell und pragmatisch

  • Du übersetzt die Roadmap in konkrete Initiativen, Business Cases und gemeinsame Ziele mit Marketing, Vertrieb und Delivery

2. Portfolio-Entwicklung (Kern der Rolle)

  • Du gestaltest unsere Portfolio-Architektur mit einer ausgewogenen Balance aus Volumen- bzw. Standardangeboten (z. B. CSP, Managed Services, SaaS, Festpreis-Pakete) und Premium- bzw. Individualleistungen (z. B. Beratung, Custom Development, BOT, End-to-End-Transformation)

  • Du produktisierst wiederkehrende Projektmuster zu skalierbaren Angeboten – und schärfst gleichzeitig die Differenzierung unserer Premiumleistungen

  • Du verantwortest Positionierung (Problem – Lösung – Nutzen), Pricing-Logik und Lifecycle der Angebote, gemeinsam mit Delivery und Technologie

3. Land-and-Expand-Modell

  • Du entwickelst Einstiegsangebote, mit denen neue Kunden einfach starten können (Land), und klare Ausbaupfade hin zu Folgeprojekten, Managed Services, Lizenzen und SaaS (Expand)

  • Du baust Programme für die Entwicklung unserer Bestandskunden auf – z. B. vom reinen Lizenzbezug zu Cloud-, Daten- und KI-Services – und gibst dem Vertrieb dafür Anlässe, Zielkundenlisten und Werkzeuge an die Hand

4. Enablement von Marketing & Vertrieb

  • Du befähigst den Vertrieb mit Playbooks, Pitch- und Angebotsvorlagen, Argumentationshilfen, Pricing-Rechnern und Schulungen

  • Du entwickelst mit Marketing Zielgruppen, Ideal Customer Profiles, Messaging und Kampagnen und sorgst für eine konsistente Story: Was machen wir, für wen, und warum Coduct?

  • Du unterstützt bei strategisch wichtigen Angeboten mit Angebotsstruktur und Pricing – die Kundenverantwortung bleibt beim Vertrieb

5. Growth-Prozesse & Steuerung

  • Du gestaltest das Growth Operating Model: Prozesse und Übergaben von Marketing über Vertrieb bis Delivery, klare Rollen und CRM-Standards

  • Du baust ein KPI-System auf – von Pipeline und Conversion über Expansion-Umsatz und Net Revenue Retention bis zum Anteil standardisierter und wiederkehrender Umsätze und zum Margen-Mix

  • Du steuerst Initiativen datenbasiert und machst Learnings teamübergreifend nutzbar

Woran wir deinen Erfolg messen

  • Umsatzbeitrag neuer und überarbeiteter Angebote

  • Expansion bei Bestandskunden (z. B. Cross-Sell-Quote, Net Revenue Retention)

  • Ausgewogener Portfolio-Mix: Anteil standardisierter/wiederkehrender Umsätze bei gesunder Marge im Premiumgeschäft

  • Wirksamkeit des Enablements: Nutzung durch den Vertrieb, Conversion und Time-to-Sale neuer Angebote

  • Umsetzung der Growth-Roadmap nach Plan

Diese Ziele bilden – zusammen mit der Wirkung auf Umsatz und EBIT der Gruppe – die Grundlage deiner variablen Vergütung.

Was du mitbringst

Erfahrung & Know-how

  • Mindestens 5 Jahre im B2B-Umfeld in Portfolio- oder Produktmanagement, Growth, Strategie, Go-to-Market oder Business Development – idealerweise in IT-Services, Cloud, Software oder Beratung

  • Portfolio-Management: Du hast Angebote entwickelt, produktisiert, bepreist und erfolgreich in den Markt gebracht

  • Land and Expand: Du hast Einstiegsangebote und Ausbaupfade gestaltet und kennst die Hebel für Wachstum im Bestand

  • Balance von Volumen und Premium: Du verstehst, wie sich Standard- und Individualgeschäft in Preis, Marge, Delivery und Vertrieb unterscheiden – und wie beide sich verstärken

  • Strategische Kompetenz: Du entwickelst Roadmaps, setzt Prioritäten und übersetzt Strategie in messbare Ergebnisse

  • Vertriebserfahrung: Du kennst Vertrieb aus eigener Praxis (z. B. Vertrieb, Pre-Sales, Key Account) und weißt, was Vertriebsteams wirklich hilft

  • Mittelstand, DACH, SaaS und CSP: Du kennst Bedürfnisse und Entscheidungswege mittelständischer Unternehmen, den DACH-Markt sowie SaaS- und Microsoft-CSP-Geschäftsmodelle

  • Prozessmanagement & Vertriebscontrolling: Du gestaltest Prozesse über Abteilungsgrenzen hinweg, arbeitest sicher mit CRM-Systemen und KPIs

  • Sprachen: Deutsch auf C2-Niveau und fließendes Englisch

Persönlichkeit & Arbeitsweise

  • Hunter-Mentalität: Du jagst neue Wachstumschancen – Segmente, Partnerschaften, Großchancen – und bringst sie mit Marketing und Vertrieb zum Abschluss

  • Ergebnisorientierung: Du willst dich an messbaren Zielen und an deiner Wirkung auf Umsatz und EBIT messen lassen – auch in der Vergütung

  • Macher:in: Du handelst proaktiv, mit Bias for Action, und lieferst Ergebnisse statt Konzepte für die Schublade

  • Einfluss ohne Weisungsbefugnis: Du überzeugst Vertrieb, Marketing, Delivery und Geschäftsführung – mit Klarheit, Daten und guten Argumenten

  • Teamplayer in verteilten Teams: Du machst andere erfolgreich, teilst Wissen offen und arbeitest gern remote, asynchron und mit unseren Kolleg:innen in Vietnam

  • Ambition zu wachsen: Du willst in den nächsten Jahren mehr strategische und Führungsverantwortung übernehmen

Wünschenswert

  • Erfahrung im Microsoft-Partner-Ökosystem (Co-Selling, Partnerprogramme, Marketplace)

  • Erfahrung mit Sales- oder Revenue-Operations und Enablement-Programmen

  • Sicherer Umgang mit KI-Tools in Analyse, Content und Enablement

Was wir dir bieten

  • Gestaltungsspielraum: Du baust die Growth-Funktion von Anfang an mit auf und arbeitest direkt mit VP Growth und Geschäftsführung zusammen

  • Leistungsorientierte Vergütung: Fixgehalt plus variable Komponente – dein Erfolg bei Growth-KPIs, Umsatz und EBIT zahlt sich direkt aus

  • Entwicklungspfad: Die Rolle ist bewusst als Sprungbrett angelegt – hin zu einer führenden Growth-Rolle in der Gruppe

  • Zukunftsthemen: Cloud, Daten, KI und eigene SaaS-Produkte – mit eigenem Delivery-Center in Vietnam

  • Kultur: ein Team, das sich gegenseitig unterstützt, ehrlich kommuniziert, pragmatisch entscheidet und kurze Wege hat

  • Flexibilität: flexible Arbeitszeiten, hybrides Arbeiten – Office Kamp-Lintfort oder Berlin (ca. 1 Tag/Woche), sonst mobil innerhalb Deutschlands; gelegentliche Reisen in der DACH-Region

So läuft der Auswahlprozess

  • Sichtung deiner Unterlagen – Rückmeldung innerhalb von 10 Werktagen

  • Erstgespräch (ca. 75 Minuten, per Video) mit VP Growth, Chief of Staff und einem Teammitglied aus Vertrieb oder Marketing

  • Fallstudie und Zweitgespräch (ca. 90 Min., per Video) mit der Geschäftsführung – du präsentierst deine Lösung einer praxisnahen Aufgabe (ca. 1 Woche Vorbereitung)

  • Angebot

Interesse?

Bewirb dich mit deinem Lebenslauf und beantworte uns kurz eine Frage: Welches Angebot hast du zuletzt so entwickelt oder geschärft, dass es spürbar mehr Umsatz gebracht hat – und wie hast du den Vertrieb dabei mitgenommen? Ein Anschreiben brauchen wir nicht. Gehaltsvorstellung und frühestmöglichen Starttermin nennst du uns gern direkt mit.

Bei uns findest du ein Team, das sich gegenseitig unterstützt und gemeinsam seine Ziele verfolgt. Wir setzen auf ehrliche Kommunikation, pragmatische Lösungen und eine Atmosphäre, in der Arbeiten Freude macht. Werde Teil unseres Teams und gestalte mit uns die Zukunft innovativer Projekte!

title: GTM
descriptionHtml:
Deducta

GTM

Location: London, UK, near London Bridge. Hybrid, 3-4 in-person days a week.

Compensation: From £120k base salary plus equity and commission (£200k+ Realistic OTE)

Visa Sponsorship: Available for the right candidate

Start Date: As soon as possible

Why we exist

Every decision a business makes, from the suppliers it trusts to the risks it accepts, eventually shows up as spend. This makes spend data the most honest record of how a company operates. Not the strategy deck or the org chart: spend describes what really happened.

This record exists, but it's scattered across dozens of systems and decades of legacy technology. Companies spending billions a year still can't easily answer: Who are our suppliers? Where are we exposed? What are we paying for twice?

We believe a business that can't see itself clearly can't make great decisions. Deducta exists to give the world's most complex organisations a true picture of how they operate, and the intelligence to act on it. Our ambition is to become the category-defining platform for enterprise data intelligence.

We're well funded, growing fast, and have already processed more than £1 trillion of spend for some of the world's largest and most recognisable companies. Our partners use Deducta to deliver major business transformations orders of magnitude faster.

Why this role matters

Our partners use Deducta to deliver major transformations, and winning them takes a consultative sale with senior executives. This role owns customer acquisition end to end, from opening relationships with C-suite and VP-level leaders to signed partnership. You'll report to the leadership team.

You'll have significant autonomy to lead sophisticated enterprise deals, work directly with client data in our platform, and build the business cases that win them. You'll carry a quota and be accountable for closing new business. As the commercial function grows, you'll be a leader in it, setting the standard for how we sell and shaping the repeatable motion behind it.

What you'll do

  • Customer acquisition: Own the full sales cycle, from identifying and engaging senior executives through to close.

  • Pipeline generation: Map target accounts, open relationships with senior stakeholders and build a pipeline of enterprises where Deducta can deliver outsized value.

  • Business cases: Build quantified business cases and materials that translate Deducta's capabilities into the outcomes decision-makers care about.

  • Complex deals: Lead multi-stakeholder deals, run product demonstrations, work with client data in the platform, and coordinate product, engineering and delivery to keep momentum.

  • Pipeline discipline: Make next steps, risks, decision-makers and deal status explicit across every opportunity.

  • Closing: Carry a quota and close new enterprise business, negotiating commercial terms and guiding deals through procurement and legal to signature.

Success in this role means:

  • Quota attainment: You consistently hit your number by creating and closing high-quality enterprise opportunities where Deducta can deliver meaningful value.

  • Deal momentum: Complex deals move forward with clear next steps, strong executive sponsorship and fewer stalls or surprises.

  • Trusted before signing: Prospects understand the business case for Deducta and see us as a credible partner before they sign.

  • Repeatable motion: You help make the commercial motion more repeatable, and others learn from how you sell.

Who you are

We're looking for a commercially minded, high-agency seller with a proven track record of closing complex, multi-stakeholder enterprise deals. You'll combine structured problem solving and analytical depth with the drive to win sophisticated enterprise customers.

You might be the right fit if you have:

  • Executive presence: You can sit across from a CPO or CFO, earn their trust and build a relationship that lasts beyond the deal.

  • Commercial judgement: You read an account, understand what matters to each stakeholder and find the best path to a decision.

  • Analytical instincts: You work directly with client data and turn the analysis into a clear, compelling business case.

  • Programme management: You coordinate complex, multi-stakeholder processes and follow through without a pre-existing playbook.

  • Product fluency: You run product demonstrations and work in the platform yourself rather than relying on others.

  • Drive to win: You have the hunger to create opportunities, sustain momentum and close business, with a record of hitting or exceeding quota.

  • Nice to have: Entrepreneurial experience, experience mentoring or leading others, or prior startup or high-growth go-to-market experience.

We care most about how you think, the quality of your work and how you approach unfamiliar problems. Previous startup experience isn't essential, but the pace, initiative and judgement to thrive in one are.

How we work

We believe in freedom and responsibility. We set clear priorities, share the context and trust people to decide how to deliver. You'll thrive here if you value:

  • Ownership: You own the outcome, not just the task. You deliver what you commit to, follow through when things get difficult, and own your mistakes.

  • Unreasonable hospitality: You treat prospects, clients and teammates with exceptional care as a default. You anticipate needs, communicate with clarity, and help others succeed.

  • Bias for action: We don’t have every answer upfront. You move things forward without waiting to be asked, take calculated risks, and adapt as you learn.

  • Craft: Moving quickly matters, but so does doing work that stays clear, reliable and useful as we grow.

  • System building: You create leverage beyond your own output, building processes, tools and documentation that others reuse and that keep working without you.

  • Candor: You tell the hard truth early, give and receive feedback thoughtfully, ask for help when you need it, and push back when priorities need to change.

  • Curiosity about AI: You’re excited by what applied AI makes possible, and you look for ways to use it in your own work.

As an early team member, you'll help shape our culture, our processes and where Deducta goes next. We're growing quickly, and this role will grow with us.

Hiring process

  1. Intro call

  2. Background interview

  3. Technical exercise

  4. Final interview

  5. Offer, referencing and start

Help the world's biggest businesses finally see themselves clearly.

THG Ingenuity is a proprietary Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) technology, robotics, and operations platform built for global ecommerce. Today, THG Ingenuity provides an integrating operating environment that enables brands to intelligently optimise the entire commerce lifecycle from browsing and checkout to AI inventory management and forecasting, automated fulfilment, carrier control, and customer experience. With its expertise in building and scaling brands, THG Ingenuity is uniquely positioned to bring pertinent, pragmatic, and global know-how across all aspects of commerce.

Hale Country Club & Spa is a private members’ destination dedicated to elevated wellbeing. Designed for those who value performance as much as restoration, it offers an environment where fitness, luxury and community coexist.

title: Hardware Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About us

Salience Labs is building the optical infrastructure that will power the next generation of AI. Our photonic switching technology delivers the high-speed, ultra-low latency networking fabrics AI datacenters need and can’t get anywhere else. We’re a multi-disciplinary team of physicists, engineers, and machine learning specialists on a mission to remove the bottlenecks holding AI infrastructure back.

Job Overview

As a Hardware Engineer at Salience Labs, you will play a crucial role in designing and testing the electronics that power our hybrid photonic-electronic systems. As an early member of the team, you will contribute directly to our mission of bringing photonic products to high-performance compute systems, particularly those used for AI.

The role offers a varied mix of system design, PCB design, system bring-up and qualification, with a significant share of hands-on lab work at our Oxford office.

title: hbo-stage Analyseren kwaliteit bouwvergunningen BAG
descriptionHtml:
hbo-afstudeerstage, vanaf februari 2027

Ben jij die nieuwsgierige en enthousiaste student die graag in data duikt en op zoek gaat naar opvallende patronen en verbanden?
Krijg jij energie van het ontrafelen van complexe vraagstukken, het ontdekken van inzichten en het vertalen van data naar betekenisvolle resultaten?

Dit is jouw uitdaging

Het CBS ontvangt maandelijks van de 342 gemeenten in Nederland informatie over verleende bouwvergunningen. Gemeenten leveren deze gegevens aan via enquêtes en registreren de bouwvergunningen daarnaast in de Basisregistratie Adressen en Gebouwen (BAG).

Sinds 2025 publiceert het CBS de cijfers over bouwvergunningen op basis van de BAG. Er is echter een groot en toenemend verschil tussen de cijfers uit de BAG en de tellingen uit de enquêtes. Er is reeds onderzoek gedaan naar deze toenemende verschillen.

Als stagiair ga je dit verder onderzoeken, door middel van een diepgaande analyse van de tijdigheid en kwaliteit van de registratie van gegevens in de BAG. Daarnaast verzamel je informatie over het registratieproces om beter inzicht te krijgen in hoe de BAG zich verhoudt tot de werkelijkheid.

Je onderzoekt onder andere:

  • Hoe lang wachten gemeenten met registraties?

  • Worden registraties doorlopend geregistreerd, of opgespaard en in korte tijd geregistreerd in de BAG?

  • Verandert de kwaliteit en tijdigheid door de tijd heen?

Om deze vragen te beantwoorden duik je in een grote database, waar je met behulp van SQL en R of Python trends gaat waarnemen, data visualiseert, en samenvattingen maakt.

Daarnaast verzamel je informatie over het registratieproces, en hoe dit is geïmplementeerd bij gemeenten. Voor deze taak is al eerder onderzoek gedaan, en is er ook al meer informatie beschikbaar. Je verzamelt deze resultaten in een rapport met een overzicht van de huidige stand van zaken.

Dit is jouw stageplek bij CBS Den Haag

Ons team bestaat uit 24 enthousiaste collega’s, die met veel passie en plezier werken aan statistische informatie over vastgoed en de woningmarkt.

We maken statistieken over (bouw)vergunningen, ontwikkeling van de woningvoorraad, (gemiddelde) WOZ-waardes, eigendomsverhoudingen, tijdelijke woningen, woningtransformaties en nog heel veel meer. We doen statistisch onderzoek op verzoek van organisaties in de publieke sector. En we beheren en verwerken data voor CBS-collega’s en werken samen met diverse organisaties, waaronder het Kadaster, de ministeries van BZK, VRO en EZK en Eurostat.

We publiceren regelmatig over de dynamiek van de Nederlandse vastgoed- en woningmarkt. Onze nieuwsberichten halen regelmatig journaals, nieuwssites en voorpagina’s van landelijke dagbladen. En daar zijn we trots op!

Dit breng jij mee

Je volgt een hbo opleiding in de studierichting toegepaste wiskunde, data science of sociale wetenschappen.

  • Je hebt affiniteit met de woningmarkt.

  • Je hebt kennis en wellicht ervaring met R/rmarkdown en/of Python en SQL databases.

  • Je bent nieuwsgierig, leergierig en enthousiast om met data aan de slag te gaan.

  • Je vindt het leuk om nieuwe dingen te ontdekken, neemt graag initiatief en denkt actief mee.

  • Je kunt zelfstandig werken, maar zoekt ook graag de samenwerking op.

  • Je deelt gemakkelijk je ideeën en bevindingen en staat open voor nieuwe inzichten en feedback.

Omdat tijdens de stage alle communicatie – zowel mondeling als schriftelijk – in het Nederlands plaatsvindt, is een goede beheersing van de Nederlandse taal noodzakelijk.

Dit kun je van ons verwachten

Een fijne leeromgeving waarin je:

  • samenwerkt met ervaren experts binnen hun vakgebied;

  • gaat werken met grote databases (SQL);

  • kennis opbouwt van de BAG en het registratieproces bij bronhouders;

  • analyses samenvat in data visualisaties en overzichtelijke tabellen.

Voor jouw inzet ontvang je een stagevergoeding van € 800,- bruto per maand (op basis van 40 uur per week).

Samen met je stagebegeleider stem je af hoe je hybride kunt werken, met flexibele werktijden en de optie om deels vanuit huis aan jouw stageopdracht te werken.

Dit zijn onze voorwaarden

Het betreft een stageopdracht en geen werkervaringsplek. Voordat je aan de stage begint verwachten we dat je vanuit de onderwijsinstelling een stagebegeleider hebt, waarmee de stage is afgestemd en concrete leerdoelen zijn afgesproken.
Deze stageopdracht is bedoeld voor studenten die momenteel staan ingeschreven bij een onderwijsinstelling; afgestudeerden komen niet in aanmerking.
